newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia backs down on labor law changes.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia backs down on labor law changes.

text.p: The British Columbia government Wednesday withdrew controversial proposed amendments to the provincial labor code after mounting opposition from the business community.
Labour Minister John Cashore announced the retreat on the front steps of the legislature and took blame for not taking the concerns of businesses and building contractors seriously.
"I think I would have to say I did not manage the launch of the bill well. I take full responsibility for that," he told reporters.
The bill would have forced all unionized construction workers into province-wide bargaining units for residential, institutional or highway construction.
Cashore said the public was more upset about the perception that the government had failed to consult with business than about the changes themselves.
"The public, especially the business community, has indicated that they are very distressed about the process. That led to misunderstandings about the content," he said.

"We are going forward with the process," he added, promising that sectoral bargaining would go to an ad hoc review panel and other changes to an advisory committee representing labor and big and small business.
He promised new legislation next year.
Cashore's announcement came on the eve of a Thursday rally before the legislature organized by the Alliance of B.C. Business, a coalition of business groups. The rally was later cancelled.
Business leaders have said the changes were aimed at rewarding unions for their support of the left-leaning New Democratic Party government by helping them to organize workers.
After the announcement, the B.C. Federation of Labour accused the government of submitting to "economic extortion by the business community."
